title: Navigating Complexity: A User-Centered Evaluation of Project Management Tools
abstract: arXiv:2611.09260v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: In the age of digital transformation, companies are increasingly relying on specialized software to manage the complexity of projects. However, when selecting tools, features and costs often take precedence over user experience (UX), leading to low adoption rates, user frustration, and project delays. This study empirically evaluates the user experience of leading project management tools (Jira, Trello, Monday.com, Asana, and Microsoft Project) across various project scales using a mixed methods approach. The System Usability Scale (SUS) was used as the primary quantitative instrument, with data collected from 141 experienced professionals via online questionnaires. The results reveal a significant trade-off between functionality and usability. translated_title: 驾驭复杂性：以用户为中心的项目管理工具评估
translated_abstract: 在数字化转型的时代，企业日益依赖专业软件来管理项目的复杂性。然而，在选择工具时，功能和成本往往优先于用户体验（UX），导致采用率低、用户受挫和项目延误。本研究采用混合研究方法，实证评估了主流项目管理工具（Jira、Trello、Monday.com、Asana和Microsoft Project）在不同项目规模下的用户体验。研究采用系统可用性量表（SUS）作为主要定量工具，通过在线问卷收集了141位经验丰富的专业人士的数据。结果揭示了功能性与可用性之间存在显著的权衡关系。Trello获得了最高的SUS得分（77.5），表明其在小型项目和敏捷团队中具有卓越的用户体验，而Microsoft Project得分最低（51.2），表明其在可用性方面存在显著的……
tldr: 本研究通过对141位专业人士的SUS量表调查，实证评估了五款主流项目管理工具的用户体验，揭示了功能性与可用性之间的显著权衡——Trello在小项目和敏捷团队中体验最佳，而Microsoft Project的可用性最差。
en_tdlr: This study empirically evaluates the user experience of five leading project management tools using SUS scores from 141 professionals, revealing a significant trade-off between functionality and usability, with Trello excelling for small projects and agile teams while Microsoft Project scores lowest in usability.
